exclusions_of_note.name: Biometric Information Exclusion
exclusions_of_note.impact: Excludes claims arising out of collection, use, storage, or disclosure of biometric identifiers/information. For a manufacturer that may use biometric time clocks, fingerprint scanners, or facial recognition for plant access, this excludes a fast-growing class of employee privacy litigation (BIPA in Illinois has produced settlements of $50M+ in single class actions; California, Texas, NY, and others now have analogous statutes). A standalone Cyber/Privacy policy with biometric coverage, or a manuscripted EPLI buy-back, would be needed to insure this exposure.

exclusions_of_note.name: Retroactive Date Limitation (Prior Acts cut to 11/30/2022)
exclusions_of_note.impact: Section II 'Full Prior Acts Coverage Provision' is deleted and replaced with a retroactive date of 11/30/2022. Any wrongful act committed before 11/30/2022 is permanently excluded. As of policy inception 11/30/2023, prior acts coverage is only 1 year — far short of typical EPLI continuity (which runs back to first inception of EPLI coverage). Long-tail employment claims (constructive discharge, harassment claims years after the conduct, retaliation tied to old protected activity) commonly arise from acts predating retro. No other policy in a typical program covers this gap.

exclusions_of_note.name: Fair Labor Standards Act Sub-Limit
exclusions_of_note.impact: Wage & hour exposure (FLSA + state-law equivalents) is subject to a sublimit rather than the full $1M aggregate. Sublimit amount is not visible on the renewal certificate. Wage & hour class actions are the single most common large-dollar employment exposure; a low sublimit (e.g., $100K–$250K defense-only) leaves a manufacturer with hourly workforce materially exposed. Sublimit amount must be confirmed against the EPL-162 form.

exclusions_of_note.name: Defense Costs Erode the Retention
exclusions_of_note.impact: Declarations and policy notice expressly state: 'Defense Costs shall be applied against the Retention.' Insured pays the first $25,000 of defense before carrier dollars engage. Standard for EPLI but worth understanding. Defense-cost-vs.-limit erosion (whether defense also erodes the $1M limit) is not visible in the renewal certificate and must be verified — most EPLI forms have defense inside the limit.

additional_findings.finding: Limit too low for a manufacturer — $1M aggregate shared across all claims
additional_findings.detail: Each Claim limit and Aggregate limit are both $1,000,000 (Pg. 9). A single discrimination, harassment, or wrongful-termination class action involving multiple claimants can exceed $1M in defense costs alone — especially in California or with a regulatory overlay. With defense costs likely inside the limit (typical for EPLI; needs confirmation from EPL-J form), a single moderately serious matter could exhaust the aggregate, leaving zero coverage for the rest of the policy year. Recommend benchmarking against employee headcount and jurisdiction; for any meaningful manufacturing workforce, $2M–$5M aggregate is more appropriate.

additional_findings.finding: Retroactive date of 11/30/2022 — only 1 year of prior acts
additional_findings.detail: EPL-148 (Pg. 11) replaces Full Prior Acts coverage with a retroactive date of 11/30/2022. As of inception 11/30/2023, only 1 year of prior wrongful acts is covered. Employment claims commonly arise long after the underlying conduct — a 2021 termination resulting in a 2024 EEOC charge would be uncovered. If Precision Aero had EPLI in prior years, the retro date should match that earliest continuous EPLI inception, not 1 year. Verify whether continuity exists; if so, push the retro back. If this is the first EPLI policy, the retro should at least step back annually (full prior acts at next renewal).

additional_findings.finding: Biometric Information Exclusion — material gap for a manufacturer
additional_findings.detail: EPL 170 (Pg. 8) excludes claims arising out of biometric information. Manufacturers commonly use biometric time clocks, fingerprint or hand-scan plant entry, and facial recognition for access control. Biometric privacy class actions under Illinois BIPA, Texas CUBI, and similar laws have produced single-employer settlements exceeding $50M. If Precision Aero uses any biometric employee identification — confirm at intake — this exclusion creates a complete coverage gap with no other policy in the program likely to respond (a Cyber/Privacy policy with affirmative biometric coverage, or a manuscripted EPLI buy-back, would be required).

additional_findings.finding: Wage & Hour sublimit (amount not disclosed on renewal certificate)
additional_findings.detail: EPL-162 (Pg. 8) sublimits FLSA / wage & hour coverage. The sublimit amount is not stated on the renewal certificate. Wage & hour is the highest-frequency, highest-severity employment exposure in most jurisdictions. For a manufacturer with hourly production employees, sublimits below $250K defense are inadequate. Action: pull the EPL-162 endorsement form to confirm the dollar sublimit, then evaluate against payroll exposure.

additional_findings.finding: Renewal Certificate only — full policy text not provided
additional_findings.detail: The document analyzed is a Renewal Certificate plus marketing inserts. The base EPLI coverage form (EPL-J), Arizona State Amendatory (EPL-AZ), Amended Definition of Loss (EPL-167), Amended Notice/Claim provisions (EPL-169), Wage & Hour sublimit (EPL-162), and Policy Jacket are all referenced but their text is not included. Several audit items cannot be confirmed from this document and require the full policy: (a) cancellation/nonrenewal notice period, (b) hammer clause/consent-to-settle structure, (c) defense costs inside vs. outside the $1M limit, (d) definition of Employee (W-2 only? temps? 1099?), (e) third-party harassment coverage, (f) punitive damages treatment, (g) wage & hour sublimit dollar amount, (h) what EPL-167 changes about the Loss definition (front pay? liquidated damages?). Recommend obtaining the full policy before final report.
USLI is a Berkshire Hathaway subsidiary with A.M. Best rating A++ (Superior) for financial stability. No carrier-financial-strength concern.
